title.narrative: Ayeyarwady Integrated River Basin Management Project

description.narrative: The objective of the Ayeyarwady Integrated River Basin Management Project for Myanmar is to strengthen integrated, climate resilient management and development of the Ayeyarwady River Basin and national water resources. There are four components to the project, the first component being water resource management institutions, decision support systems and capacity building. This component includes four subcomponents: institutional component, Ayeyarwady River Basin Master Plan and Decision Support System, Preparation of Future Investments (PFI), and implementation support. The second component is the hydro-meteorological observation and information systems modernization. This component includes three subcomponents: institutional and regulatory strengthening, capacity building and implementation support, modernization of observation infrastructure, data management systems and forecasting, and enhancement of Hydromet service delivery systems. The third component is the navigation enhancement on the Ayeyarwady River. This component includes four subcomponents: navigation Improvements, navigation aids, water quality monitoring, and institutional strengthening and implementation support. Finally, the fourth component is the contingent emergency response. This ‘zero component’ (initially without any allocated funding) will allow for the rapid reallocation of funds from other components to provide emergency recovery and reconstruction support in the event of a natural disaster, emergency and/or catastrophic event. Funds potentially reallocated to component four will be disbursed either against a positive list of critical goods and/or against the procurement of works, and consultant services required to support the immediate response and recovery needs of the GoM. A contingent emergency response implementation plan will be developed to guide financial management, procurement, safeguard and any other necessary implementation arrangements and procedures.

The program development objective for the Series of Projects (of which the AIRBM will be the first) is to strengthen integrated,climate resilient management and development of the Ayeyarwady River Basin and national water resources. The project development objective of the AIRBM is to contribute to the development of integrated river basin management on the Ayeyarwady river, and, in the event of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, to provide immediate and effective response to said Eligible Crisis or Emergency.

title.narrative: Grievances registered related to delivery of project benefits addressed

comment.narrative: <p>G??????????????????rievance redress mechanisms for the project included record keeping and handling of complaints, suggestions and requests related to project activities – whether they were received verbally and/or in writing. Regular visits were made tomonitor safeguard compliance at seasonal river training hotspots, civil works and building construction sites. The PMU and the implementing agencies including local/regional offices of DWIR conducted consultations and provided information to the affected communities on where and how to address complaints. All grievances were registered and handled appropriately.</p>

title.narrative: Component 1.3. Preparation of Feasibility Studies for Future Investments

comment.narrative:
<p>This Intermediate Results Indicator is defined as: "<em>equivalent to, or more advanced than a pre-feasibility study (relative to scope and quality)"</em><strong><em>. </em></strong>During MTR the scope of the PFI was made more specific and two feasibility studies were defined; (i) Yangon IWRM Project and (ii) Ayeyarwady Navigation Enhancement Works: Feasibility Study Engineering Design for Stretch 1 & pre-feasibility study for Stretch 2. </p>

<p>At project close, two analytical studies forming the foundation for the larger Yangon IWRM project were completed: the <em>Pan Hlaing Vision </em> and the Netherlands-supported <em>Yangon Regional Water Security Study (RWSS)</em>. The Feasibility Study for the Yangon IWRM Project itself never took off. </p>

<p>The Feasibility Study Engineering Design for Stretch 1 was completed in January 2021. </p>

title.narrative: Component 3.1 Channel stabilization Works for Sub-project 1 completed

comment.narrative: <p>River stabilization works for "sub-project 1" in the stretch of the Ayeyarwady River between Mandalay and Nyaung-U (Stretch 1) were completed in June 2021 and successfully passed the defect liability period. DWIR has conducted hydrographic surveys to assess the changes in the bathymetry of the main navigation channel and the anabranches were river works were installed, to assess the effectiveness of the interventions. </p>

title.narrative: Component 2.3 The development of site-specific weather forecasts

comment.narrative: <p>DMH is now able to issue localized weather forecasts to 18 cities, compared to 3 cities before the project. The weather forecast has, thus, been extended to cover more than 10 million people, up from about 6.6 million.</p>

title.narrative: Component 3.3: DWIR Re-organization and Operations Plan

comment.narrative: <p>The consultancy supposed to inform the re-organization of DWIR was underway when the disbursements were put on hold, hence no tangible results were reported at project close. </p>

title.narrative: Component 1.4: NWRC and its institutions legalized

comment.narrative:
<p>This IRI was added under the 2019 restructuring. </p>
<p>At project close there is no progress observed regarding the institutionalization of the NWRC. The legal anchoring of the NWRC as inter-ministerial apex body under Myanmar Law was supposed to be arranged through enactment of the Water Law and Water Resources Law. A draft version of the Water Law and Water Resources Law wasprepared, and the World Bank’s comments were shared with the Government, but a final version could not be completed. </p>

<p>Out of the total of 203 automatic weather and water level monitoring stations planned to be funded under the project, the project completed the installation of only 100 hydro-met stations purchased under the IRM (component 4) and 2 upper-air weather balloons were made operational under component 2 of the project. Equipment for another 101 stations has arrived in Myanmar but could not be installed due to the portfolio wide disbursement pause following the military takeover.</p>

<p>Under the 2019 restructuring, the target for capacity building was increased from 500 to 1500 people in anticipation of the longer project duration after restructuring. Although capacity building targets were on track at the time of the MTR, the revised target proved to be overambitious for the second half of the project. By the project closing, 559 people had been trained, far short of th revised target.</p>

<p>The target for female participation was also increased under the 2019 restructuring (from 40% to 50%), based on the high participation of female experts in the development of the Basin Masterplan and the high ratio of women staff in DMH working on the project. Achievement at project close was 49% female presence in capacity building activities compared to the target of 50%. While this is below the target, it can still be considered as a solid performance given the position of women in Myanmar society.</p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: Component 3: Improved Navigation between Mandalay and Yangon to desired operating standards

comment.narrative: <p>The project achieved its outcome of enhancing navigation on the Ayeyarwady River by providing DWIR with the tools and capacity to modernize its operations and piloting measures innovative to the river basin. This outcome was assessed via one PDO-level indicator; “Improved Navigation between Mandalay and Yangon to desired operating standards” and three Intermediate Results levelIndicators (IRIs) supporting the achievement of the PDO. 80% of project activities contributing to the PDO Indicator outcome were implemented successfully. The remaining 20% were shifted to the proposed Additional financing as Component 3 lacked the funds to implement all planned activities. </p>

title.narrative: Component 1: River Basin Master Plan Developed

comment.narrative: <p>The PDO-level indicator to measure this outcome was “River Basin Masterplan Developed” which was achieved at output level in December 2020. However, when looking at it from an indicator outcome perspective, it was not possible to fully achieve its goal of adopting Integrated Water Resources Management in the basin due to the non-materialization of certain institutional reforms such as the enactment of the Water Law and the functioning of the NWRC as a inter-ministerial apex body on integrated water resources management and continuing with the multi-stakeholder process.</p>

title.narrative: Component 1.2 : Ayeyarwady River Basin Decision Support System

comment.narrative: <p>Ayeyarwady River Basin Decision Support System (DSS) is a functional decision support system, fit for purpose for multi-sectoralbasin planning, including hydrologic, hydraulic, and water quality models coupled with GIS based user interface. The DSS was completed in December 2020 and handed over to DWIR as temporary custodian.</p>
<p>The Concept of Operations (CONOPS) including the detailed design for the upgrade of DMH's hydro-met system was finalized by April 2018.</p>

title.narrative: Component 1.1: River Basin Master Plan - State of the Basin Assessment Report

comment.narrative: <p>The State of the Basin Assessment (SOBA) report, which was published in 2018, served as the foundation for the Ayeyarwady Basin Master Plan. The SOBA was the first time a comprehensive water resources assessment was done for Myanmar and helped planners to gain a better understanding of the state of the Ayeyarwady river basin and the status and (historic) trends in key environmental, social and economic parameters of the Ayeyarwady system.</p>

<p>Navigation aids (river buoys with top lighting) were installed in the stretch of the river between Mandalay and Nyaung-U tofacilitate year round day-and-night navigation. The second batch of Aids to Navigation (AtN), which was added during the 2019 restructuring, for installation in the stretch of the river between Nyaung U and Yangon was shifted to the proposed Additional Financing as project funds were inadequate to fund this activity under the parent project. Since the Additional Financing was put on hold, no progress was made with regards to installation of the second batch of AtN, accounting to roughly 60% of the total length of the river between Yangon and Mandalay.</p>

title.narrative: Goods procured and distributed as outlined in the CERIP

comment.narrative: <p>Under a level II restructuring in June 2016, the IRM was triggered and US$3.2 million equivalent of funding from the other threeproject components was allocated to the CERC and used to purchase and install 90 Automatic Weather Observation Stations (of which 41 stations for DMH) and 10 Automatic Water Level Recording Stations (all for DMH). The new stations helped DMH to shift from manual recording to automatic data transmission of hydro-met data.</p>

title.narrative: Component 2: Improved DMH weather and climate services

comment.narrative: <p>The November 2020 post-Monsoon Forum was the last one held before the project close, following a disbursement pause. The forum reported a user satisfaction index of 65.5%, which was calculated based on Stakeholders' feedback on the usefulness, lead-time, and accuracy of forecasts and warnings issued by DMH. This index is determined through surveys conducted at the Monsoon Forums held annually in April/May and November. The Monsoon Forum 2018 established the baseline for the index at 45%.</p>
